payload.name: ExtractNamedObjectBenefitMemory
payload.description: When a user explicitly says a named object, pet, or item helps them or brings them joy, extract a memory candidate during construction.
content: When a user explicitly says a named object, pet, or item helps them or brings them joy, extract a memory candidate for that attachment; casual praise is still durable evidence.
Capture the object type and the specific benefit stated (focus, joy, comfort) as evidence-linked memory content under preference or relationship.
If the named object already appears in existing memory, issue an UPDATE/MERGE to add the new evidence instead of creating a duplicate.

solves: An explicit first-person statement that a named object/pet helps the user or brings joy was ignored during extraction, so no memory was persisted. The reusable mechanism: such benefit attributions are durable evidence of user preference/relationship and should be extracted regardless of casual phrasing. Applies to any future message where a user credits an object, pet, or item with focus, joy, comfort, or support.
